title: The next shift starts with the evidence
scenario: Hypothetical equipment-maintenance investigation at Northbank Packaging
audience: Operations leaders and engineering teams considering a pilot
timing_basis: Editorial estimates; retime after measured narration and actual interaction captures

shots.title: A small change on a busy shift
shots.narration: At Northbank Packaging, the next shift is about to begin. One cooling pump sounds different. Before anyone plans more work, the team needs to understand what has changed.
shots.visual_direction: Slow shoulder-height move along a quiet industrial aisle towards one blue pump skid. No sparks, emergency lights or people touching machinery.
shots.screen_action: Add P-204 and the film title in the edit; hold the opening disclosure legibly for the full shot.
shots.on_screen_copy: The next shift starts with the evidence | Hypothetical workflow · synthetic data
shots.capture_acceptance: Generated geography matches H02 and H03; no baked-in lettering or fabricated product UI.
shots.fallback: Use a licensed industrial still with a slow crop and the same disclosure.
shots.presenter_cue: Open with the operational problem. Do not introduce the repository names yet.

shots.title: The evidence is scattered
shots.narration: The clues are spread across a technician’s observation, an earlier work record, two versions of a maintenance reference and a trend. Finding the files is only the start. Someone must check that they concern the same asset, and decide which version applies now.
shots.visual_direction: Four readable document cards on a neutral desk-like canvas. Bring the two revision cards into the same frame; keep their dates visible.
shots.screen_action: Reveal OBS-204-01, WO-1187, MAN-P204-B and MAN-P204-C; add the illustrative trend as a small fifth card.
shots.on_screen_copy: One asset. Several records. Two document revisions.
shots.capture_acceptance: All titles, dates and IDs match scenario.json. Trend visibly says synthetic; no physical units or alarm threshold.
shots.fallback: Use static cards with sequential highlights.
shots.presenter_cue: Let the viewer read the revision letters before the next cut.

shots.title: The technician reports an observation
shots.narration: Maya records what she has noticed. In this proposed application, her spoken report becomes an incident draft she can correct before saving. The report is an observation; it does not become a diagnosis simply because an assistant transcribed it.
shots.visual_direction: Over-shoulder tablet framing, then a large transcript card. Avoid a recognisable commercial UI. Keep Maya away from moving equipment.
shots.screen_action: Show the character line as a staged input. Highlight P-204 for confirmation, then the state Reported — cause unconfirmed.
shots.on_screen_copy: Application concept · staged | Reported — cause unconfirmed
shots.capture_acceptance: Voice-to-incident flow remains labelled staged until real input, transcript correction and stored-incident evidence exist.
shots.fallback: Presenter reads the observation over the transcript card; no simulated recording waveform.
shots.presenter_cue: Pause after the character line; invite the audience to notice the distinction between observation and conclusion.

dialogue.speaker: Maya
dialogue.text: Pump P two-oh-four sounds different again. Can we bring the records together before planning more work?

shots.title: Give the records a common subject
shots.narration: The first connection is the asset itself: P two-oh-four, part of cooling loop two, serving packaging line two. Each record points to that same subject. This lets the team follow the evidence without relying on similar filenames or somebody remembering where a document lives.
shots.visual_direction: Build a small left-to-right relationship view. Maximum seven visible nodes. Distinguish the pump, system and documents by shape as well as colour.
shots.screen_action: Select P-204, then reveal its loop, line and attached records in that order.
shots.capture_acceptance: Relationships come from the fixture, with no unsupported claim of automatic discovery or a live digital twin.
shots.presenter_cue: Say what the connections mean; avoid flying through a large unreadable graph.

shots.title: Make the source inspectable
shots.narration: The foundation is editable knowledge with explicit references. Ontomark supplies tools to validate and build that material. For this pilot, the asset vocabulary and source links would be prepared deliberately. A successful structure check helps keep the model coherent; the engineer still has to judge the evidence.
shots.visual_direction: Record a small demo Markdown note beside its source references, then an actual validation result. Crop to the content being discussed.
shots.screen_action: Open NOTE-204 and show its asset identity. Run the supported validation command on a disposable, mapped demo corpus; preserve the real result.
shots.on_screen_copy: Software capture · synthetic data — only after capture acceptance
shots.capture_acceptance: Record exact command, build revision, mapped fixture and output. A passing result must not be renamed engineering approval.
shots.fallback: Show the authored fixture note with Application concept · staged; omit terminal success graphics.
shots.presenter_cue: Keep the technical insert short. The point is inspectability, not CLI fluency.

shots.title: Find the current reference
shots.narration: Here is the detail that changes the discussion. The earlier work record cites revision B. Revision C was issued later and is now the current reference in our scenario. The old record remains useful history. The next job needs the current reference.
shots.visual_direction: Side-by-side B and C cards. Animate one supersedes arrow from C to B. Keep the earlier work record linked to B.
shots.screen_action: Show 20 October on WO-1187 and 28 October on revision C. Do not alter the historical work record.
shots.on_screen_copy: B: historical reference | C: current in this scenario
shots.capture_acceptance: Supersession is a declared fixture relationship and application policy, not a claim of automatic industrial document control.
shots.presenter_cue: This is the story’s main reveal. Allow a full reading pause.

shots.title: Explore the relationship, not a guess
shots.narration: A graph view makes that relationship easier to inspect. Follow the pump to the previous work, then to the reference it used. Bring the newer reference alongside it. The picture helps people ask a better question; the links themselves still need owners, sources and review.
shots.visual_direction: Use VisionClaw’s real graph surface only after loading a verified demo mapping. Fixed camera; reveal one edge at a time.
shots.screen_action: Select the asset and inspect its linked evidence. Keep labels readable; use the actual available controls.
shots.on_screen_copy: Software capture · synthetic data — after verification | Relations, not a physical simulation
shots.capture_acceptance: Selection, labels and evidence content must be visible in the actual frame. Record loader/mapping and build identity.
shots.fallback: Use G03 with the Application concept · staged label; do not composite fake controls over a product screenshot.
shots.presenter_cue: Give the viewer a moment to follow the old-reference path.

shots.title: From scattered papers to a shared view
shots.narration: The aim is a shared view of the situation: what happened, what the records say, and where the team still needs an answer.
shots.visual_direction: Slow move from the same pump housing to a nearby meeting area. Match-cut the circular housing to the selected graph node in the edit.
shots.screen_action: Add no holographic interface to the generated frame. The graph match-cut is an editorial device.
shots.capture_acceptance: Same pump colour, aisle and lighting as H01. No suggestion that a generated scene measures machine state.
shots.fallback: Use a second crop of the establishing still, then cut to the diagram.
shots.presenter_cue: Leave a breath before the question-and-answer sequence.

shots.title: Ask a bounded question
shots.narration: Sam asks what changed around P two-oh-four, and which records deserve attention. Loom provides retrieval and grounding information that an application can use. Our proposed screen puts the answer beside its sources, so Sam can open the earlier work record and the newer reference rather than accepting a summary on trust.
shots.visual_direction: Start with the exact Q1 text, then show a real recorded retrieval response if available. Use an editorial annotation beside the response, never inside it.
shots.screen_action: Open each cited source. Show the corpus identity in a small technical inset, not as a main user task.
shots.on_screen_copy: What changed around P-204, and which records should we review?
shots.capture_acceptance: A dedicated demo corpus is loaded; the request, response and visible references agree. Scripted answer cards remain staged.
shots.fallback: Display the Q1 answer from the fixture as Application concept · staged; do not fabricate a service response.
shots.presenter_cue: If presenting live, ask the question once and leave the actual response visible.

shots.title: Keep the unanswered question visible
shots.narration: Then comes the harder question: did the last seal replacement cause the new problem? These records do not establish that. The proposed application should say so and keep the question open. An observation after a maintenance event is a reason to investigate, not proof of what caused it.
shots.visual_direction: One clear question and one short answer. Retain the two evidence references underneath; no confidence gauge.
shots.screen_action: Show Q2 and its scripted answer. Keep Cause not established visible.
shots.on_screen_copy: Cause not established by the available records
shots.capture_acceptance: Treat the refusal wording as an application requirement until its real consumer policy and negative case are tested.
shots.fallback: Presenter states the missing evidence over the source cards.
shots.presenter_cue: Do not replace this moment with a confident diagnosis to make the demo look smoother.

shots.title: Review the exact knowledge change
shots.narration: Sam reviews a narrow correction to the knowledge note: retain the old reference as history, identify revision C as current, and leave the cause unconfirmed. The proposed wording is visible before any decision. The useful question is whether this exact change is justified by the sources on screen.
shots.visual_direction: Show the exact NOTE-204 before/after text as a readable diff. A real proposal surface may be used only when it displays the same scope and content.
shots.screen_action: Highlight the revision correction first, then the explicit unresolved-cause sentence. Leave identity fields unchanged.
shots.on_screen_copy: Review this note change | Cause remains unconfirmed
shots.capture_acceptance: The displayed proposal identifies NOTE-204 and matches its fixture content. UI approval alone cannot certify application.
shots.fallback: Use a labelled review-rehearsal diff; keep real product chrome out of the mock-up.
shots.presenter_cue: Read the changed sentence aloud. Do not approve a hidden bundle of edits.

shots.title: Separate a decision from its effects
shots.narration: There are three different states to show: proposed, reviewed, and applied. A review decision does not prove that a file changed, or that the next reader has the new version. The pilot should retain a separate record for each step and show a failure when one of those steps does not complete.
shots.visual_direction: Three large state cards with a separate receipt beneath each. Initially stop at reviewed; keep applied unfilled.
shots.screen_action: Advance Proposed to Reviewed. Do not animate Applied until CAP05 supplies evidence, or label the whole sequence staged.
shots.on_screen_copy: Proposed → Reviewed → Applied | Separate evidence for each step
shots.capture_acceptance: Any connected success needs content/subject/digest agreement and actual output. Known audit gaps must not be concealed by animation.
shots.fallback: Keep all three cards as an explanatory diagram with the staged label.
shots.presenter_cue: Explain this in everyday language: deciding and doing are different events.

shots.title: Hand a plan to the responsible person
shots.narration: The outcome is an investigation plan, owned by Sam and handed to Alex for planning. The team’s normal maintenance process still governs scheduling, permits and physical work. In this first rehearsal, the handoff is manual. A connection to a maintenance-management system would be a separate integration to implement and verify.
shots.visual_direction: Show PLAN-204 with owner, planner, current reference and open question. End on a clearly labelled manual handoff.
shots.screen_action: Reveal owner Sam, planner Alex and the plan’s actual text. No work-order-created toast or machinery command.
shots.on_screen_copy: Investigation plan | Manual handoff | Cause still open
shots.capture_acceptance: The plan remains a proposal for authorised planning; no external system success or equipment action is implied.
shots.fallback: Use a readable document page and presenter handoff.
shots.presenter_cue: Answer who owns the next step; avoid implying that the software authorises physical work.

shots.title: Verify the supported change
shots.narration: Applying the correction should leave two things the team can inspect: the changed note and a record of the change. If the reviewed passage has changed in the meantime, the update must stop for another look. The handover should contain only the wording that was actually reviewed.
shots.visual_direction: Record a disposable single-note application and its output, then show the resulting diff. Include a short separate stale-context refusal take for production review.
shots.screen_action: Use only a prepared demo repository and the supported writer command. Preserve the full receipt off-screen.
shots.on_screen_copy: Applied note + actual receipt — only if verified
shots.capture_acceptance: Inspect output bytes and subject/digest agreement. A direct CLI capture does not establish the full Agentbox-to-review-UI integration.
shots.fallback: Show a staged before/after document with Manual rehearsal, not a fabricated application receipt.
shots.presenter_cue: In the live presentation, narrate the actual result rather than reading a success line automatically.

shots.title: Leave a useful handover
shots.narration: The handover is now specific. The observation is still open. Revision C is the reference to use. Sam reviewed the note correction; Alex owns planning. The cause remains unconfirmed. The next shift receives that account, with links back to the records, instead of having to reconstruct the conversation.
shots.visual_direction: Full-screen HANDOVER-204 card with five short lines and source links. No completion checkmark on the incident.
shots.screen_action: Read down observation, reference, reviewer, next owner and unresolved cause.
shots.on_screen_copy: Open observation · Current reference · Reviewed change · Next owner · Open question
shots.capture_acceptance: Every field matches the fixture. Any receipt link shown as clickable must resolve to actual captured evidence or remain visibly staged.
shots.fallback: Use the handover text as a document slide.
shots.presenter_cue: Hold the card. This is the practical deliverable of the story.

shots.title: The next shift can ask again
shots.narration: Leah arrives on the next shift and asks what she needs to know about P two-oh-four. The intended application gives her the reviewed handover, with the unresolved question intact. She can see who owns the next step and open the evidence herself, without finding everyone who joined the earlier conversation.
shots.visual_direction: Ask Q3 in a fresh session. Show the actual answer and an opened updated note side by side.
shots.screen_action: Record a fresh query after verified consumer refresh. Compare its served identity with the captured update.
shots.capture_acceptance: Capture proves refreshed serving state and the same updated note. No reuse of the earlier Q1 recording as a new response.
shots.fallback: Use the scripted Q3 card labelled Target behaviour · staged.
shots.presenter_cue: Ask a different person to explain the next action using only the handover.

shots.title: Reveal the small technical spine
shots.narration: Behind the story are a few distinct jobs. Ontomark manages the authored knowledge. Loom selects context for a request. Agentbox provides agent execution and supported change adapters. VisionClaw provides graph and review surfaces. The industrial application has to join those jobs with the site’s own rules and prove each handoff.
shots.visual_direction: Four labelled component cards around a central Evidence and decisions card. Add a separate dashed Application integration band.
shots.screen_action: Reveal component jobs one at a time. Keep inspection, review and physical maintenance as separate concepts.
shots.on_screen_copy: Authored knowledge · Grounding · Agent work · Graph and review
shots.capture_acceptance: Diagram is labelled proposed composition. No arrow is presented as a currently tested complete industrial connection.
shots.fallback: Use the same four cards without animation.
shots.presenter_cue: This is the only stack overview. Refer technical questions to research.md.

shots.title: Invite a measurable pilot
shots.narration: Start with one asset, one recurring question and a small team. Measure how long it takes to find the right evidence, review a correction and hand it on. The next shift should inherit the reasoning, as well as the record.
shots.visual_direction: Return to the same quiet aisle with a slight change of daylight. End on a clean title card over the frame.
shots.screen_action: Do not show a repaired machine, a green production dashboard or an avoided-downtime number.
shots.on_screen_copy: One asset. One question. A traceable handover.
shots.capture_acceptance: Closing image suggests continuity, not an unmeasured repair or performance result.
shots.fallback: Reuse a short approved H01 clip and a deterministic end card.
shots.presenter_cue: End by proposing the bounded pilot, then take questions.
